question: In a suspected fire death, which combination of PM findings BEST confirms that the burns were sustained ante-mortem (vital reaction present)?

answers.text: Pugilistic (boxer's) attitude + charring of extremities + intact internal organs

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Incorrect. Pugilistic attitude results from heat-induced muscle protein coagulation and occurs in both ante-mortem and post-mortem burns — it is NOT a vital reaction sign.

answers.text: Carbon monoxide (CO) in blood (>50% carboxyhaemoglobin) + serum blisters + PMN infiltration at burn margins

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Correct. Vital reaction in burns is confirmed by: (1) elevated COHb (>50% indicates significant inhalation while alive), (2) serum blisters (require an active inflammatory response during life), and (3) PMN leucocyte infiltration at burn margins (histological gold standard). The pugilistic attitude is NOT a vital reaction.

answers.text: Absence of soot in airways + skin charring + adipocere formation

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Incorrect. Absent soot in airways actually suggests post-mortem fire exposure (the person wasn't breathing during the fire). Adipocere is a late change related to decomposition, not vital reaction.

answers.text: Skin splitting at joints + dessication of tissues + cherry-red skin discolouration

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Incorrect. Skin splitting and dessication are heat artefacts. Cherry-red discolouration is from CO poisoning but alone does not confirm ante-mortem burns — it must be combined with other vital reaction signs.

overallFeedback.feedback: Vital reaction in ante-mortem burns: (1) COHb >50% — the person was breathing smoke; (2) Serum (not steam) blisters — require live inflammatory response; (3) PMN leucocyte infiltration at margins — histological proof. Pugilistic attitude = heat artefact, not vital reaction.
Correct. Vital reaction in burns = COHb >50% in blood + serum blisters + PMN infiltration. Pugilistic attitude is a heat artefact, NOT vital reaction.
